name: Implementation Shortfall Abort
note: Perold's decomposition used as an entry rule rather than an accounting one. At the decision bar the close is recorded as P0 and the expected edge as k_edge*ATR/P0; the order is then worked over n_slice bars, each slice filling at that bar's (H+L+C)/3, and the running shortfall of the fills against P0 is tracked. Three branches: shortfall above phi_abort*edge cancels the remainder and the trade never happens; a favourable shortfall accelerates and takes the position immediately; otherwise the schedule completes and the position is taken on the last slice. The shared harness fills atomically, so 'cancel the remainder' becomes 'do not participate' and the partial-fill sizing of the published rule is not expressible here - that substitution is deliberate and is the one thing lost.
source: Perold, A.F. (1988), 'The Implementation Shortfall: Paper versus Reality', Journal of Portfolio Management 14(3), 4-9. Complemented by Almgren & Chriss (2000), which uses expected shortfall and its variance as the objective throughout.
code:
def _atr(h, l, c, p):
    n = len(c)
    tr = [0.0] * n
    if n:
        tr[0] = h[0] - l[0]
    for j in range(1, n):
        pc = c[j - 1]
        a = h[j] - l[j]
        b = pc - h[j]
        if b < 0.0:
            b = -b
        d = pc - l[j]
        if d < 0.0:
            d = -d
        tr[j] = a if (a >= b and a >= d) else (b if b >= d else d)
    out = [None] * n
    if n < p or p < 1:
        return out
    s = 0.0
    for j in range(p):
        s += tr[j]
    s /= p
    out[p - 1] = s
    for j in range(p, n):
        s = (s * (p - 1) + tr[j]) / p
        out[j] = s
    return out


def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    o = [float(x["o"]) for x in b]
    h = [float(x["h"]) for x in b]
    l = [float(x["l"]) for x in b]
    c = [float(x["c"]) for x in b]
    atr = _atr(h, l, c, max(2, int(ctx.p.atr_n)))

    dc = max(2, int(ctx.p.dc_n))
    ns = max(1, int(ctx.p.n_slice))
    phi = float(ctx.p.phi_abort)
    ke = float(ctx.p.k_edge)

    # ---- the base decision: an N-bar breakout. Any signal would do; this one
    # fires often enough that the abort branch is what is being measured. ----
    base = [0] * n
    for j in range(dc, n):
        hh = h[j - dc]
        ll = l[j - dc]
        for k in range(j - dc + 1, j):
            if h[k] > hh:
                hh = h[k]
            if l[k] < ll:
                ll = l[k]
        if c[j] > hh:
            base[j] = 1
        elif c[j] < ll:
            base[j] = -1

    sig = [0] * n
    filled = [0] * n        # 1 = schedule completed, 2 = accelerated
    aborts = 0
    j = 0
    while j < n:
        d = base[j]
        if d == 0:
            j += 1
            continue
        a = atr[j]
        p0 = c[j]
        if a is None or a <= 0.0 or p0 <= 0.0:
            j += 1
            continue
        edge = ke * a / p0                 # expected edge, as a fraction
        acc = 0.0
        cnt = 0
        fired = -1
        why = 0
        end = j + ns
        if end >= n:
            end = n - 1
        k = j + 1
        while k <= end:
            acc += (h[k] + l[k] + c[k]) / 3.0
            cnt += 1
            shortfall = d * (acc / cnt - p0) / p0
            if shortfall > phi * edge:
                # the market has already taken phi of the edge before the
                # order is done: cancel the remainder, permanently
                break
            if shortfall < 0.0:
                fired = k          # accelerate -- finish the whole remainder
                why = 2
                break
            if cnt >= ns:
                fired = k          # schedule completed on time
                why = 1
                break
            k += 1
        if fired >= 0:
            sig[fired] = d
            filled[fired] = why
            j = fired + 1
        else:
            aborts += 1
            j = end + 1
    ctx.log("aborted %d of the scheduled orders" % aborts)
    ctx.sg = ctx.series(sig, "is_abort_sig")


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.sg[i]
    return s if s else 0
